title: Multidimensional Perioperative Pain Trajectories
official: Multidimensional Perioperative Pain Trajectories: A French Prospective Registry
summary: Chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP), recognised as a distinct clinical entity in ICD-11, adopted in 2019, represents an important public health concern. It is defined as pain that develops or increases in intensity following surgery and persists beyond the healing process, for at least three months. Despite advances in postoperative pain management over recent decades, CPSP remains a concern in both adults and children, with its frequency varying according to the surgical procedure and patient characteristics. Its development involves interacting physical, psychological and perioperative factors. This French registry aims to characterise multidimensional perioperative pain trajectories and identify their determinants.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children aged \>7 years or adults.
* Ability to complete self-report assessments.
* Completion of the online preoperative questionnaires.
* Scheduled elective surgery associated with a risk of chronic postsurgical pain: Spinal surgery , Thoracotomy, Inguinal hernia repair, Cesarean section, Mastectomy, Cholecystectomy, Coronary artery bypass grafting, Limb amputation, Joint arthroplasty or Craniotomy

Exclusion Criteria:

* Refusal to participate.
